title: Token Waste Reinforcing Loop
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking
Causal Loop Diagrams
Reinforcing Loop
Balancing Loop
Token Budgets
description: Interactive causal loop diagram with two linked loops built from this book's token-waste example. Reinforcing loop R: unnecessary parallel agents pay startup overhead, which reduces the tokens remaining in the window, which raises the pressure to rush, which launches more unnecessary agents. Balancing loop B: the same overhead draws chapter token budgeting, which raises cost awareness, which reduces unnecessary agents. Selecting a loop highlights its path, traces one change around it, and counts its negative links.

educational.topic: Reinforcing and balancing feedback loops in token use
learningObjectives: Differentiate a reinforcing loop from a balancing loop using this book's own token-waste example.
Trace a change around a causal loop using link polarities.
Classify a loop as reinforcing or balancing by counting its negative links.
prerequisites: Knows that each additional agent pays a fixed startup overhead
Has read about token waste antipatterns and chapter token budgeting

equations: Loop type = reinforcing when the number of negative links on the loop is even, balancing when it is odd
assumptions: Each link is a qualitative claim about direction of change, not a measured relationship
Roughly 12,000 tokens of startup overhead per agent is the figure measured on this project
limitations: Does not model magnitudes, delays, or how strongly one loop dominates the other

pedagogical.pattern: Comparison of two structures with traced worked example
pedagogical.teachingStrategy: The learner selects each loop in turn, follows one change around it, and compares where the change ends up
keyQuestions: Does a change come back amplified or reversed after one trip around the loop?
How many negative links does each loop have, and what does that tell you?
commonMisconceptions: A reinforcing loop always describes something good, and a balancing loop something bad
A minus sign on a link means the effect is harmful
assessmentOpportunities: Classify each loop and justify the classification with the count of negative links
